score_scale.0: Demonstrated failure or required behavior demonstrably absent

domains.name: Solutions Architecture

criteria.name: Requirements and constraints
criteria.level_3_requirement: Architecture addresses stated users, data, scale, cost, latency, and risk constraints that matter to the project

criteria.name: Boundaries and contracts
criteria.level_3_requirement: Components have clear responsibilities; dependencies and interfaces support the intended changes
github_evidence: architecture diagrams reconciled with imports and calls

criteria.name: Failure and data flow design
criteria.level_3_requirement: Important failure paths, consistency needs, and trust boundaries have explicit handling

criteria.name: Tradeoffs and evolution
criteria.level_3_requirement: Choices are proportionate and alternatives, cost implications, and likely changes are addressed

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2 example: the main workflow has understandable components, but dependency failure and data ownership are unclear. Level 4 example: a documented choice between a simple service and a queue-based design is supported by representative failure or load results. Elaborate architecture alone earns no bonus.

domains.name: Human Centered Design

criteria.name: User and task understanding
criteria.level_3_requirement: Identifies intended users, their goals, and meaningful workflow constraints

criteria.name: Interaction and feedback
criteria.level_3_requirement: Main journeys provide clear navigation or commands, useful status, and actionable errors

criteria.name: Accessibility and inclusion
criteria.level_3_requirement: Supports relevant keyboard, semantic, visual, language, and assistive interaction needs

criteria.name: Recovery and user control
criteria.level_3_requirement: Users can understand consequential actions, correct mistakes, and recover from relevant failures
github_evidence: AI citations or uncertainty where relevant

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2 example: a usable happy path exists but errors discard input or lack recovery. Level 4 requires evidence from representative usability or accessibility checks and resulting improvements. Attractive screenshots alone do not establish usability; automated accessibility scans alone do not establish conformance.

domains.name: Product Management

criteria.name: Problem and value
criteria.level_3_requirement: Clearly defines the user problem, intended outcome, and meaningful constraints

criteria.name: Prioritization and scope
criteria.level_3_requirement: Scope addresses the main user outcome and handles dependencies and exclusions coherently

criteria.name: Acceptance and success measures
criteria.level_3_requirement: Important features have testable acceptance criteria and appropriate outcome measures

criteria.name: Feedback and iteration
criteria.level_3_requirement: Changes respond to credible feedback or measured behavior and document the resulting decision

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2 example: the product purpose and feature scope are clear, but success measures and feedback are missing. Level 4 requires a traceable feedback-to-decision-to-change cycle with an assessed outcome. Instrumentation code establishes measurement capability, not actual customer value or adoption.

domains.name: AI Collaboration and Verification

criteria.name: Task decomposition and context
criteria.level_3_requirement: AI-assisted tasks have usable goals, constraints, interfaces, and completion checks

criteria.name: Review and technical ownership
criteria.level_3_requirement: Contributor can explain material decisions and identifies or corrects unsuitable AI output

criteria.name: Independent verification
criteria.level_3_requirement: Uses checks that can expose mistakes rather than accepting the AI's own claim of correctness

criteria.name: Safe and efficient delegation
criteria.level_3_requirement: Delegates with appropriate permissions, data boundaries, checkpoints, and resource limits

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2 example: AI tasks and resulting code are documented with basic checks, but correction and ownership are not demonstrated. Level 4 requires an attributable cycle in which the contributor finds a consequential AI error, revises the approach, and validates the correction while explaining tradeoffs. A repository-only review often leaves C4 partially unknown. Do not assume AI was used because instructions or generated-looking code exist.

domains.name: Software Development

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.level_3_requirement: Implements required behavior and important boundary conditions

criteria.name: Maintainability
criteria.level_3_requirement: Responsibilities, naming, and abstractions make likely changes understandable

criteria.name: Error and resource handling
criteria.level_3_requirement: Handles errors and manages connections, files, memory, and asynchronous work appropriately

criteria.name: Dependencies and contracts
criteria.level_3_requirement: Dependencies and types or schemas are intentional, compatible, and reproducible

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: main behavior is implemented with limited boundary handling. Level 4: measured or observed maintenance problems are reduced through verified changes without unnecessary abstraction.

domains.name: API and Integration Design

criteria.name: Contract clarity
criteria.level_3_requirement: Inputs, outputs, errors, and compatibility are explicit

criteria.name: Access boundaries
criteria.level_3_requirement: Authentication and object-level authorization protect relevant operations

criteria.name: Resilience
criteria.level_3_requirement: Relevant timeouts, rate limits, retries, and failure fallbacks are bounded

criteria.name: Consistency and evolution
criteria.level_3_requirement: Handles pagination, duplicate requests, partial results, and changes where relevant

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: a working integration covers normal responses. Level 4: representative outages, duplicate delivery, and compatibility changes are tested with observed results.

domains.name: Database Design

criteria.name: Schema and integrity
criteria.level_3_requirement: Schema fits access patterns and protects required invariants

criteria.name: Query design
criteria.level_3_requirement: Important queries and indexes are appropriate to expected usage

criteria.name: Transactions and concurrency
criteria.level_3_requirement: Multi-step writes preserve relevant invariants under concurrent access

criteria.name: Lifecycle and recovery
criteria.level_3_requirement: Schema changes, retention, and recovery match the project's needs

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: basic CRUD and schema exist, with incomplete integrity or migration handling. Level 4: realistic query, concurrency, migration, or recovery evidence validates key design choices.

domains.name: Data Engineering

criteria.name: Ingestion contracts
criteria.level_3_requirement: Validates schemas and handles missing, malformed, and changing inputs

criteria.name: Repeatable processing
criteria.level_3_requirement: Retries and reruns avoid corruption or unintended duplication

criteria.name: Quality and lineage
criteria.level_3_requirement: Records source provenance and checks relevant quality properties

criteria.name: Operations and scale
criteria.level_3_requirement: Handles expected volume, scheduling, and failed records appropriately

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: a pipeline processes a clean example dataset. Level 4: repeatable results under late, duplicate, malformed, and representative-volume inputs validate the pipeline.

domains.name: Data Analytics

criteria.name: Metric semantics
criteria.level_3_requirement: Defines grain, population, time windows, denominators, and exclusions

criteria.name: Analytical correctness
criteria.level_3_requirement: Handles joins, nulls, time zones, aggregation, and filtering correctly

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.level_3_requirement: Visualizations and explanations accurately answer the intended question

criteria.name: Decision support
criteria.level_3_requirement: Conclusions distinguish observations, uncertainty, and causal claims

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: useful queries and charts exist but definitions or reconciliation are incomplete. Level 4: validated metrics and sensitivity analysis support a traceable decision.

domains.name: Data Science

criteria.name: Problem and baseline
criteria.level_3_requirement: Uses an appropriate objective, metric, and meaningful baseline

criteria.name: Experimental validity
criteria.level_3_requirement: Splits and preprocessing prevent relevant leakage and support the use case

criteria.name: Reproducibility
criteria.level_3_requirement: Data versions, environment, configuration, and experiments can be reconstructed

criteria.name: Error and uncertainty analysis
criteria.level_3_requirement: Analyzes important error slices, uncertainty, and generalization limits

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: a model trains and reports an appropriate metric on a basic split. Level 4: comparisons, error analysis, and valid uncertainty estimates substantiate improvements beyond the baseline.

domains.name: AI Implementation

criteria.name: Model and task fit
criteria.level_3_requirement: Model and prompting choices fit requirements with a simpler baseline considered

criteria.name: Output and tool contracts
criteria.level_3_requirement: Validates structured output and constrains tools before consequential use

criteria.name: Behavioral evaluation
criteria.level_3_requirement: Uses representative normal, edge, and adversarial cases with explicit grading

criteria.name: Runtime control
criteria.level_3_requirement: Controls latency, spending, failures, and sensitive logging

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: the model powers the main experience with basic error handling. Level 4: representative held-out evaluation and cost or latency results justify choices and show improvement. API integration alone does not establish AI quality.

domains.name: RAG and Knowledge Base Design

criteria.name: Ingestion and freshness
criteria.level_3_requirement: Preserves provenance and supports appropriate updates and deletions

criteria.name: Retrieval quality
criteria.level_3_requirement: Evaluates retrieval against relevant questions and reference evidence
github_evidence: recall at k or ranking metrics

criteria.name: Grounded answers
criteria.level_3_requirement: Supports answers with correct citations and handles insufficient evidence

criteria.name: Access and hostile content
criteria.level_3_requirement: Enforces document permissions and treats retrieved instructions as untrusted

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: documents can be indexed, retrieved, and cited in the main scenario. Level 4: separate retrieval and answer evaluations demonstrate improvements while maintaining permission and freshness controls.

domains.name: Workflow Automation

criteria.name: States and transitions
criteria.level_3_requirement: Workflow states, triggers, dependencies, and completion criteria are explicit

criteria.name: Retry and duplication control
criteria.level_3_requirement: Retries are bounded and duplicate events do not repeat consequential actions

criteria.name: Human control and audit
criteria.level_3_requirement: Consequential actions have suitable authorization, review, and traceability

criteria.name: Partial failure recovery
criteria.level_3_requirement: Can resume, reconcile, or compensate after important failures

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: the normal sequence completes. Level 4: interruption, duplicate delivery, and partial failure exercises demonstrate safe recovery.

domains.name: Automated Testing

criteria.name: Risk-based coverage
criteria.level_3_requirement: Tests cover important requirements at suitable unit, integration, and end-to-end levels

criteria.name: Assertion strength
criteria.level_3_requirement: Assertions can expose meaningful defects and verify outcomes beyond mocks
github_evidence: mutation or seeded-defect results where useful

criteria.name: Test realism
criteria.level_3_requirement: Test doubles and fixtures preserve relevant contracts; important real boundaries are exercised

criteria.name: Reliability and reproducibility
criteria.level_3_requirement: Tests run deterministically enough for their purpose with clear setup and isolation

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: the main path is tested with useful assertions. Level 4: evidence shows the suite catches representative regressions and remains reliable. Coverage percentage or test count alone cannot establish this.

domains.name: Automated Quality Assurance

criteria.name: Repeatable release checks
criteria.level_3_requirement: Required checks cover relevant quality risks and block or explicitly handle failure

criteria.name: Breadth of quality checks
criteria.level_3_requirement: Checks address applicable security, accessibility, performance, and AI risks

criteria.name: Defect lifecycle
criteria.level_3_requirement: Defects have reproducible reports, severity, correction, and verification

criteria.name: Traceable release evidence
criteria.level_3_requirement: Results correspond to the evaluated revision and release artifact

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: CI runs basic checks. Level 4: release evidence and defect history demonstrate that the process detects escapes and improves. A workflow YAML does not prove a run passed or a branch protection rule is enabled; inspect run results and repository settings when accessible.

domains.name: Security and Privacy

criteria.name: Identity and authorization
criteria.level_3_requirement: Relevant authentication and per-object or tenant access are enforced

criteria.name: Input and execution boundaries
criteria.level_3_requirement: Untrusted input cannot cross relevant query, rendering, execution, or AI tool boundaries unchecked

criteria.name: Secrets and dependencies
criteria.level_3_requirement: Credentials are kept out of committed code and dependency risks are managed

criteria.name: Data lifecycle
criteria.level_3_requirement: Collection, storage, logs, retention, and deletion protect relevant sensitive data

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: basic controls exist with incomplete negative testing or lifecycle handling. Level 4: a proportionate threat model and targeted tests validate important defenses. Do not copy exposed credentials into a report; redact and reference the location.

domains.name: Deployment and Operations

criteria.name: Reproducible setup
criteria.level_3_requirement: A clean environment can run the intended deliverable with documented configuration

criteria.name: Delivery and rollback
criteria.level_3_requirement: Release and recovery are appropriate to the deployment model

criteria.name: Observability
criteria.level_3_requirement: Relevant health, errors, latency, and costs can be diagnosed without leaking data

criteria.name: Recovery and capacity
criteria.level_3_requirement: Important outages and expected workload are addressed proportionately

domains.domain_level_examples: Level 2: the author can run and deploy the application with some manual setup. Level 4: clean setup and representative recovery or workload exercises substantiate operating assumptions.
